bear: Large, short-tailed, shaggy animal that feeds on plants as well as small animals. The bear mentioned several times in the Bible is the Syrian brown bear still found in Syria and Turkey but no longer in Israel.
bebai: 1. Ancestor of a family that returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel after the exile.
bela: 1. Beor’s son, a king of Edom who ruled before Israel had a king.
ben: Hebrew word often used as a prefix to describe a relationship. Literally meaning “son,” it is found some 4,850 times in the OT.
benjamin: 1. Youngest of Jacob’s 12 sons and full brother to Joseph.
bered: Alternate name for Beker, one of Ephraim’s sons, in 1 Chronicles 7:20.
bethel: Pagan deity mentioned in ancient texts and thought by some to have biblical reference.
bethuel: Youngest son of Abraham’s brother Nahor and his wife, Milcah. Bethuel was thus Abraham’s nephew.
bethuel, bethul: One of the cities allotted to Simeon’s tribe within Judah’s inheritance.
bible, manuscripts and text of the: Bible, Manuscripts and Text of the

Copies of the OT books produced by scribes and editions made from these copies. The ancient manuscripts of the OT are the basic working material used to seek out the original text of the Bible with as great a degree of accuracy as possible.
bible, versions of the: To get a picture of how the Bible has come to different peoples in the world, spread out a map of the eastern hemisphere and imagine Palestine as the center of a pool.
bilhah: Servant given by Laban to his daughter Rachel when she married Jacob. Realizing her own childlessness, Rachel gave Bilhah to her husband as a concubine and accepted their two sons as her own, naming them Dan and Naphtali (30:3-8; 35:25; 46:25).
boaz: Salmon’s son of Judah’s tribe. Boaz lived in Bethlehem in the days of the judges and married Ruth, a Moabite woman.
bosor: KJV form of Beor, Balaam’s father, in 2 Peter 2:15.
brothers: Designation of those in the household of God. Good evidence exists that Jews at the time of Jesus frequently referred to themselves as brothers.
buz: 1. Abraham’s nephew, and one of Nahor’s eight sons.
cain: First son of Adam and Eve, who became a tiller of the soil while his brother, Abel, was a keeper of sheep. Cain’s murder of Abel became proverbial of similarly violent and destructive sins.
cherub: One of five Babylonian cities from which Israelites who could not trace their ancestry returned after the exile.
chronology of the bible: Branch of biblical studies that attempts to assign dates and sequences to OT events. Chronology is a science.
dan: Fifth son of the Jewish patriarch Jacob. Dan’s mother was Bilhah, maid of Jacob’s wife Rachel.
daniel: 1. David’s second son, the first by his wife Abigail; also called Kileab.
debir: One of the kings of Eglon who became an ally of Adoni-zedek, the king of Jerusalem. Debir was executed by Joshua.
dedan: 1. Grandson of Cush in the list of Noah’s descendants.
didache: A manual of church discipline, otherwise known as “The Teaching of the Lord to the Gentiles through the Twelve Apostles.” Its origin and date are difficult to determine precisely, but scholars generally agree that it was written in Syria or Palestine during the late first century or early second century.
dumah: Ishmael’s son, who founded an Arab tribe.
eder: 1. Member of Benjamin’s tribe and the son of Beriah, a leader in the town of Aijalon.
eglon: Moabite king who captured Jericho and held it for 18 years, exacting a tribute from Israel. Ehud, an Israelite judge pretending to bring tribute, killed Eglon.
elam: 1. Firstborn son of Shem and a grandson of Noah.
elon: 1. Hittite who was the father of Basemath (perhaps also called Adah, Gn 36:2), one of Esau’s wives (26:34).
enoch: 1. Cain’s son and grandson of Adam.
ephah: Measure of grain, about half a bushel (18 liters).
ephod: Upper garment worn during religious services associated with the tabernacle or temple. “Ephod” generally referred to the ornamented vest that the high priest wore over a blue robe.
ephraim: Joseph’s younger son, born of Joseph and Asenath before the seven years of famine in Egypt. He was the ancestor of an Israelite tribe, and his name came to designate the northern kingdom of Israel.
ephrath: Mother of Hur and Caleb’s second wife.
ephron: Hittite from whom Abraham purchased the cave of Machpelah with its adjoining field for 400 shekels of silver. Sarah was buried there, as was Abraham (25:9) and Jacob (50:13).
eshcol: Amorite who, with his brothers Mamre and Aner, helped the patriarch Abraham defeat the forces of Kedorlaomer and rescue Lot and his family.
eshtemoa, eshtemoh: City south of Jerusalem allotted to Judah when Palestine was divided among the 12 tribes. Eshtemoa was assigned to the Levites.
esther: One of two names borne by the Jewish queen of Persia. Hadassah (Hebrew “Myrtle”) apparently was her Jewish name, and Esther (Persian “Star”) her name as queen of Persia.
ezekiel: Priest and prophet during Israel’s Babylonian exile. Ezekiel was a descendant of the influential priestly family of Zadok.
ezra: 1. Religious reformer following Israel’s return from exile.
finger: Linear measure equivalent to the width of a finger.
gad: 1. One of the 12 sons of Jacob.
gedor: Jeiel’s son, who was an ancestor of King Saul. Gedor’s family lived in Gibeon.
gilead: 1. Makir’s son from Manasseh’s tribe and head of the clan of his descendants (26:29; 27:1) during the time of Moses (36:1).
habakkuk: Author of the eighth book of the Minor Prophets. The meaning of Habakkuk’s name is uncertain.
haggai: Prophet whose book is the 10th in a series of 12 brief prophetic books concluding the OT. Haggai’s name probably came from a word for “festival.” We have no information concerning his family or social background.
ham: Second son of Noah. Ham had four sons whose names were Cush, Mizraim (Hebrew for Egypt), Put, and Canaan.
hammath: Ancestor of the house of Rechab, about whom nothing else is known.
haran: 1. Terah’s son, brother of Abraham, and the father of Lot.
hebron: 1. Third of Kohath’s four sons, Hebron was a descendant of Levi.
hepher: 1. Manassite and founder of the Hepherite family.
hezron: 1. Reuben’s son and founder of the Hezronite family in Reuben’s tribe.
hosah: Merarite Levite who guarded the gate of the tent where the sacred ark was kept when David brought it to Jerusalem. His gatekeeping responsibilities were shared by his sons (26:10-16).
hosea: Prophet of ancient Israel whose sphere of activity was the northern kingdom. Little is known of him outside of the prophetic book that bears his name.
immer: Priest in the time of David. He became the ancestral head of a house of priests: Pashhur, the priest who had Jeremiah arrested and placed in stocks, was a descendant of Immer.
isaiah: Eighth-century BC prophet during the reigns of the Judean kings Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah; author of the biblical book of Isaiah. Isaiah was the son of Amoz and may have been a relative of King Amaziah.
israel: Name meaning “one who struggles with God” or “God struggles” (Gn 32:28, NLT mg). It was given to Isaac’s son Jacob and to his descendants (35:9-12; cf.
jabesh: Shallum’s father. Shallum assassinated Zechariah, king of Israel.
jabesh, jabesh-gilead: Town appearing in the closing chapters of the book of Judges (chs 19–21).
jabez: Member of Judah’s tribe who was noted for his godliness. He prayed for God’s protection, and his prayer was answered.
james: 1. James, brother of Jesus; leading elder in the church at Jerusalem; author of the epistle bearing his name.
japhia: 1. King of Lachish who joined an alliance of four other Amorite kings to punish Gibeon for its treaty with the Jews.
javan: Japheth’s son whose seafaring descendants migrated to the north and west of Canaan.
jehoshaphat: 1. The fourth king of Judah (872–848 BC), son and successor of Asa (910–869 BC).
jeremiah: 1. Prophet to Judah before its fall in 586 BC; his name is also spelled “Jeremias” and “Jeremy” in the KJV.
jeshua: 1. Levite and head of the ninth of 24 divisions of priests formed during David’s reign.
jesse: Son of Obed and grandson of Ruth and Boaz. Jesse was a shepherd from Bethlehem.
jezreel: 1. Descendant of Etam from the tribe of Judah.
job: 1. KJV rendering of Iob, an alternate form of Jashub, Issachar’s third son, in Genesis 46:13.
joel: 1. Levite from the family of Kohath.
john: 1. Father of Simon Peter and Andrew.
jonah: Prophet of Israel; Amittai’s son of the Zebulunite city of Gath-hepher. The historian who wrote 2 Kings recorded that Jonah had a major prophetic role in the reign of King Jeroboam II (793–753 BC).
joshua: 1. Son of Nun, Moses’ assistant and successor, and the military leader whom God chose to lead the Israelites in the conquest of Canaan (Nm 13:16, KJV “Jehoshua”; also spelled “Jehoshuah” in 1 Chr 7:27 and “Jeshua” in Neh 8:17).
juda: 1. Alternate KJV spelling of Judas, Jesus’ brother, in Mark 6:3.
judah: 1. Fourth of Jacob’s 12 sons and the fourth son born to Jacob by Leah, who, overjoyed with the thought of bearing Jacob another son, named him Judah, meaning “praise”.
jude: Brother of James and author of the general epistle named Jude. Jude is the English form of the Greek name Judas (Hebrew Judah).
judith: 1. Daughter of Beeri the Hittite and one of Esau’s wives.
kain: Town in the Judean hill country. Its place in the same district as the known cities of Maon, Carmel, Ziph, and Juttah (v 55) favors its identification with Khirbet Yuqim, southwest of Hebron.
keilah: Caleb’s descendant from Judah’s tribe, called the Garmite in 1 Chronicles 4:19. Some identify this reference with the city in Judah instead of a person.
laban: Bethuel’s son, brother of Rebekah (vv 15, 29), father of Leah and Rachel (29:16), and the uncle and father-in-law of Jacob.
laish: Father of Paltiel (Palti), to whom Saul gave his daughter Michal, who was formerly David’s wife.
luke: Companion of the apostle Paul; author of the third Gospel and Acts.
lydia: Gentile woman who was converted under the preaching of Paul in Philippi. Lydia was a dealer in purple cloth and came from the city of Thyatira in the region of Lydia in the western part of the Roman province of Asia (commonly known as Asia Minor).
maacah, maachah: Common Hebrew name, often spelled Maachah in the KJV.
madmannah: Shaaph’s son and a grandson of Caleb.
mahalath: Musical cue, perhaps meaning “sadness,” listed in the title of Psalm 53 (see RSV), which would designate the way in which and/or the melody to which the psalm should be sung.
malachi: Author of the last book of the OT. The prophet Malachi lived about 500–460 BC.
mamre: Owner of a parcel of land called “the plain of Mamre.” He was an Amorite and is recorded as having two brothers: Aner and Eshcol. These became confederates of Abraham when he fought to save his nephew Lot.
manasseh: 1. Firstborn son of Joseph and his Egyptian wife, Asenath.
maon: Chief town in the hill country of Judah, about nine miles (14.5 kilometers) south of Hebron. David and his men hid in this area while fleeing from Saul, and David’s wife Abigail was from this town (25:2-3).
mareshah: 1. Caleb’s firstborn son and the father of Hebron (1 Chr 2:42; RSV, based on the Greek text).
matthew: Son of Alphaeus; a tax collector by occupation; chosen by Jesus to be one of the 12 apostles; credited with the authorship of the Gospel of Matthew.
mesha: 1. King of Moab in the ninth century BC whose name is derived from a root meaning “to save or deliver.” According to 2 Kings 3:4-5, Mesha was a sheep breeder who paid heavy tribute to Israel during the time of Ahab but rebelled after Ahab’s death.
micah: 1. Ephraimite judge who had idols made and then hired a Levite to become his priest.
naamah: 1. Daughter of Zillah and Lamech in the list of Cain’s descendants.
naarah: One of Ashhur’s two wives, who bore him four sons.
nahor: 1. Abraham’s grandfather; also an ancestor of Jesus according to Luke’s genealogy (Lk 3:34, where some English translations follow the Greek spelling, Nachor).
nahum: 1. A prophet of Judah whose name means “consolation” or “consoler.” This name fits his message, as he wrote to encourage the people of Judah while they were being oppressed by the Assyrians.
naphtali: One of Jacob’s 12 sons. He was the second of two sons borne to Jacob by Bilhah, Rachel’s maid.
narcissus: Christian whose household knew the Lord and received greetings from Paul in his letter to Rome.
nebo: Marduk’s son and a chief god among the Babylonian pantheon. Nebo (Hebrew spelling; pronounced Nabu in Akkadian) was the patron deity of wisdom, education, and literature.
nehemiah: Name of three men mentioned in the OT after the period of the exile. The name means “the Lord comforts” and was appropriate for this time of hope and fulfillment.
nobah: Manassite who conquered and settled the town of Kenath, east of the Jordan, and subsequently renamed it after himself.
on: Reubenite, Peleth’s son who joined Korah’s rebellion against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness.
ophir: Joktan’s son and a descendant of Shem through Arphaxad’s line.
pace: Linear measure equivalent to the average distance of a man’s stride, or about one yard (.9 meter).
penuel: 1. Descendant (possibly son) of Hur and father (in the sense of progenitor) of Gedor from Judah’s tribe.
peor: Contraction for the Canaanite god of Baal-peor, or for the place itself.
philemon: Christian known only from the letter addressed to him by the apostle Paul. He is mentioned nowhere else in the NT.
put: Third of Ham’s four sons, who most likely settled in northern Africa and is perhaps the forefather of the peoples of Egypt and Libya.
rahab: Mythological sea monster that poetically represented Egypt. “For Egypt’s help is worthless and empty, therefore I have called her ‘Rahab who sits still’ ” (Is 30:7, RSV).
rameses: Alternate form of the Egyptian Ramses of the 19th and 20th dynasties.
ramoth: KJV form of Jeremoth, Bani’s son, in Ezra 10:29.
ramses: Name of 11 kings of the 19th and 20th Egyptian dynasties (also spelled Rameses). Ramses II reigned for some 67 years (c. 1290–1224 BC).
rehob: 1. King of Zobah whose son, Hadadezer, was defeated by David at the Euphrates River.
rekem: 1. Prince or king of Midian killed with his four accomplices in a battle waged by Moses at the Lord’s command.
reuben: Eldest son of Jacob and Leah and forefather of one of the 12 tribes of Israel. Reuben was involved in the mandrake incident (30:14) and had sexual relations with Bilhah, his father’s concubine (35:22).
rimmon: 1. Benjaminite of Beeroth, whose two sons, Baanah and Recab, assassinated Ishbosheth.
ruth: Moabitess and the widow of Mahlon, the son of Naomi and Elimelech, who were Ephrathites from Bethlehem living in Moab because of a severe famine in Judah.
salmon: Nahshon’s son and an ancestor of David from Judah’s tribe. Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab and is listed in Matthew’s genealogy as a forefather of Jesus Christ; in the Greek his name is spelled Sala in Luke’s genealogy.
samuel: Last of the judges, his name means “name of God” or “his name is El” (El is the name of the God of strength and power). The play on words in 1 Samuel 1:20 (cf.
seir: Father of seven sons and a descendant of Abraham through Esau’s line. Originally a Horite tribe dwelling in the land of Edom, the nation descended from Seir was first dispossessed by, but later intermarried with, Esau’s descendants.
sheba: 1. Son of Raamah, the brother of Dedan and a descendant of Noah through Ham’s line.
shema: 1. Judahite, Hebron’s son and a descendant of Caleb.
shimron: Issachar’s fourth son and the founder of the Shimronite family.
shittim: Site on the plains of Moab where the Israelites made their final Transjordan encampment after defeating Sihon and Og and prior to their crossing of the Jordan (25:1).
shual: Zophah’s son and a leader in Asher’s tribe.
sidon: Canaan’s firstborn son; Canaan was the son of Ham and grandson of Noah. Sidon founded a city (bearing his name) that set the northern boundary of the land of Canaan and later played a dominant role in Palestinian history.
simeon: 1. Second of the 12 sons of Jacob and the second son borne to him by Leah.
soco: Son of Heber, listed in the genealogy of Caleb. Since the Calebites were located in the southern hill country of Judah, Soco may be identified with the city in Joshua 15:48.
solomon: Third king over Israel, the second son of David and Bathsheba, who reigned 40 years (970–930 BC). His alternative name was Jedidiah, “beloved of the Lord.”
tabor: City mentioned in 1 Chronicles 6:77 in a list of the towns of Zebulun. In a similar list in Joshua 19:12 the city is named Kisloth-Tabor; if the same city is meant, the Chronicler may have abbreviated the name here.
tahath: 1. Son of Assir and a descendant of Levi through Kohath’s line.
tamar: 1. Wife of Er, the firstborn son of Judah by a Canaanitess.
tappuah: Hebron’s son and a descendant of Caleb from Judah’s tribe.
tarshish: 1. One of Javan’s four sons and a descendant of Noah through Japheth’s line.
tebah: Son of Abraham’s brother Nahor. His mother was Reumah, Nahor’s concubine.
telem: One of the gatekeepers who was encouraged by Ezra to divorce his foreign wife.
tema: Ninth son of Ishmael who became chief of a powerful nomadic tribe in the north Arabian wilderness. The descendants of Tema were primarily caravan traders who controlled access to important routes across the desert.
teman: One of the chiefs of the Edomites and Eliphaz’s firstborn son. He was likely either the founder or a chief of the Edomite city of Teman.
terah: Father of Abram (Abraham), Nahor, and Haran. Though Abram is listed first among his sons, it is likely that Abram was not the oldest.
timna: 1. Daughter of Seir, sister of Lotan, and a native Horite inhabitant of Edom.
timnah: 1. One of the cities on the northern boundary of Judah’s inheritance, located between Beth-shemesh and Ekron.
timothy: Paul’s convert and companion, whose name means “one who honors God.”
tirzah: One of the daughters of Zelophehad of Manasseh’s tribe. Since her father had no sons, she and her sisters asked for and received their father’s inheritance.
titus: 1. One of Paul’s converts—“my true child in a common faith” (Ti 1:4, NASB)—who became an intimate and trusted associate of the apostle in his mission of planting Christianity throughout the Mediterranean world.
tobit: Primary character of the deuterocanonical book of Tobit.
ur: Father of Eliphal, one of David’s mighty men; probably the same as Ahasbai in the parallel passage.
uz: 1. Aram’s firstborn son and a descendant of Shem.
uzal: Son of Joktan, a descendant of Eber through Shem’s line.
yahweh: Most holy name for God in the OT, usually translated “LORD.” See God, Names of (Yahweh).
zalmon: One of David’s mighty men; alternately called Ilai the Ahohite in 1 Chronicles 11:29.
zanoah: Descendant of Caleb from Judah’s tribe. Zanoah was the son of Jekuthiel and, depending on the translation of the Hebrew text, may have been related to Bithiah, the daughter of Pharaoh.
zebulun: One of Jacob’s 12 sons. He was the sixth and last son borne to Jacob by Leah, who named the boy Zebulun, meaning “abode, dwelling,” for she said, “Now my husband will dwell with me, because I have borne him six sons” (Gn 30:20, NASB, emphasis added).
zechariah: Extremely popular name in the Bible; it means “the Lord remembers.”
zephaniah: 1. Priest during the reign of Zedekiah who was executed at Riblah by the king of Babylon.
zimri: 1. Clan chief of Simeon’s tribe who was killed by Phinehas for consorting with a Midianite woman at Peor.
ziph: 1. Descendant of Caleb from Judah’s tribe.
zuph: Ancestor of Elkanah, the father of the prophet Samuel. Zuph was a member of the Kohathite branch of Levites and is listed as the son of Elkanah (different than above) and the father of Toah.
